(women's)]]''' }} }} '''Olympique de Marseille''' ({{IPA|fr|ɔlɛ̃pik də maʁsɛj|lang}}, {{IPA|fr|olɛ̃ˈpikə də maχˈsɛjə|label=[[Meridional French|locally]]|generic=yes}}; {{langx|oc|Olimpic de Marselha}}, {{IPA|oc|ulimˈpi de maʀˈsejɔ|pron}}), also known simply as '''Marseille''', or by the abbreviation '''OM''' ({{IPA|fr|oɛm|}}, {{IPA|fr|oˈɛmə|label=locally|generic=yes}}), is a French professional [[Association football|football]] club based in [[Marseille]] which competes in [[Ligue 1]], the [[French football league system|top flight]] of [[Football in France|French football]]. Marseille play their home matches at the [[Stade Vélodrome]].{{cite web | url=http://www.om.net/en/Club/502001/Stade_Velodrome | title=Velodrome Stadium | publisher=om.net | access-date=13 January 2008 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080228054349/http://www.om.net/en/Club/502001/Stade_Velodrome | archive-date=28 February 2008 | url-status=dead | df=dmy-all }} OM is one of the most popular football clubs in the country, having regularly averaged the highest attendance in French football. They have a long-standing rivalry with [[Paris Saint-Germain F.C.|Paris Saint-Germain]], against whom they contest [[Le Classique]]. Behind PSG, Marseille is the second most decorated French football team with a total of 29 trophies, including [[Football records and statistics in France#Total titles won (1918–present)|28 major titles]]. They have won 26 domestic trophies: nine [[List of French football champions|league]] titles, one [[Ligue 2]] title, ten [[Coupe de France]], one [[Coupe Charles Drago]], three [[Coupe de la Ligue]], and three [[Trophée des Champions]]. Internationally, OM won the [[UEFA Champions League]] in [[1992–93 UEFA Champions League|1993]], becoming the first French side to claim the trophy and one of just two French clubs to secure a [[List of UEFA club competition winners|major European title]].{{cite news|url=https://www.lequipe.fr/Football/FootballFicheClub6.html|title=Ligue 1 - Olympique de Marseille|website=[[L'Équipe]]|access-date=8 June 2023|language=French|archive-date=21 May 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210521191216/https://www.lequipe.fr/Football/FootballFicheClub6.html|url-status=live}} The [[UEFA Intertoto Cup]] in [[2005 UEFA Intertoto Cup|2005]] marked the club's second continental triumph. They were also runners-up at the European Cup (currently the Champions League) in [[1990–91 UEFA Champions League|1991]] and at the [[UEFA Europa League]] (formerly the UEFA Cup) in [[1998–99 UEFA Cup|1999]], [[2003–04 UEFA Cup|2004]] and [[2017–18 UEFA Europa League|2018]].{{cite news|url=https://www.lequipe.fr/Football/Actualites/Avant-la-ligue-europa-2018-les-precedentes-finales-de-l-om/898016|title=Avant la Ligue Europa 2018, les précédentes finales de l'OM|website=[[L'Équipe]]|date=4 May 2018|access-date=8 June 2023|language=French|archive-date=3 September 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230903180341/https://www.lequipe.fr/Football/Actualites/Avant-la-ligue-europa-2018-les-precedentes-finales-de-l-om/898016|url-status=live}} American businessman [[Frank McCourt (executive)|Frank McCourt]] bought 95% of the club's stake in 2016 and Marseille was listed in the [[Deloitte Football Money League]] at the end of the 2023–2024 season,
